title: MontuPython Desktop
tagline: Astronomical ephemerides for the ancient world
paragraphs: MontuPython computes astronomical ephemerides thousands of years before the present — developed for ancient Egypt and useful at any archaeoastronomical site. MontuPython Desktop is its graphical front-end: open a module from the sidebar to run predefined calculations. Each module also offers Python code you can copy into your own projects.

modules.title: Calendar Calculator
modules.description: Convert dates among Julian/Gregorian, proleptic Gregorian, caniucular (Egyptian civil), Julian Day, and historical presets.

modules.title: Observer Location
modules.description: Set the observer site (predefined ancient locations, map click, or manual coordinates). Shared by all sky modules.

modules.title: Sky Map
modules.description: Azimuthal sky maps with precessed stars, asterisms, ecliptic, horizon, and solar-system bodies.

modules.title: Seasons & Lunar Phases
modules.description: Exact dates of the four astronomical seasons and all lunar phases for any historical year.

modules.title: Planetary Ephemerides
modules.description: Plot sky-condition properties for the Sun, Moon, and classical planets over a chosen time span.

modules.title: Orientation Disk
modules.description: Extreme rise and set azimuths for the Sun, planets, and stars on an azimuth disk (N at top).

modules.title: Star Alignments
modules.description: Find which bright stars passed through a fixed azimuth and elevation over a date range, with precession.

modules.title: Heliacal Rises
modules.description: Find first visible morning appearances of named stars and planets using Schaefer or Belokrylov visibility models. For a list of historical Sirius heliacal rises see this link.

configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.save: Saves all module parameters and the observer location to your personal settings file (config.json). Restored automatically on the next launch.
configuration.reset: Restores factory defaults from default.json and overwrites config.json. Use this to start fresh.
